newsitem.title: USA: ACLU sues Pa. county for poor public defense program.
newsitem.headline: ACLU sues Pa. county for poor public defense program.

text.p: The American Civil Liberties Union has filed a class-action lawsuit against Allegheny County for failing to provide adequate representation for poor criminal defendants, ACLU officials said Wednesday.
The county salary board, the three county commissioners and its chief public defender were named as defendents.

ACLU officials said the public defence office was so ill equipped that defendants were being deprived of legal protections guaranteed by the U.S. and Pennsylvania Constitutions. It charges that the county allowed the office to deteriorate.
"This is not a case against the public defenders," said Vic Walczak, director of the ACLU Pittsburgh chapter at a news conference. "They are forced to work without adequate resources."

Allegheny County covers Pittsburgh and surrounding towns. The suit was filed in commmon pleas court on behalf of three indigent clients, but aims to apply to all current and future cases that public defenders will handle.
The suit does not seek monetary damages but rather reform in the public defence office. It alleges the office is underfunded and its lawyers so overburdened they cannot adequately handle their cases.
"When I say minutes, I literally mean minutes that public defenders meet with their clients prior to a hearing," Jere Krakoff, a civil rights lawyer, told reporters.

The office was found to be inadequate 10 months ago in an American Bar Association study. Its budget was cut by about one-third this year and the office currently has 45 lawyers, down from 55 last year. All of the lawyers are paid part-time salaries.
